# Fail-Closed PowerShell Plan: Recursive Directory Move Within a Workspace

## Step 1 — Resolve and validate the workspace root first

Resolve the workspace root with `Resolve-Path` and fail immediately if it doesn't exist or isn't a container. This establishes the trusted boundary everything else is checked against.

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$workspace = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Work\MyWorkspace' -ErrorAction Stop
if (-not $workspace.Path) { throw 'Workspace root could not be resolved.' }
```

## Step 2 — Resolve the source path and verify it exists and is inside the workspace

Resolve the source directory, confirm it is a directory, and verify its full path starts with the workspace root (plus a separator, to prevent sibling-directory prefix collisions like `C:\Work\MyWorkspace2`).

```powershell
$source = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Work\MyWorkspace\SubDir\TargetDir' -ErrorAction Stop
if (-not ($source.Path -eq $workspace.Path -or
          $source.Path.StartsWith($workspace.Path + [IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar))) {
    throw "Source escapes workspace: $($source.Path)"
}
if ((Get-Item -LiteralPath $source.Path).PSIsContainer -ne $true) {
    throw 'Source is not a directory.'
}
```

## Step 3 — Resolve the destination parent and verify it is inside the workspace and does not already contain the target

Resolve the destination parent directory, apply the same containment check, and fail closed if a directory with the target name already exists there (avoiding silent merge or overwrite).

```powershell
$destParent = Resolve-Path -LiteralPath 'C:\Work\MyWorkspace\Archive' -ErrorAction Stop
if (-not $destParent.Path.StartsWith($workspace.Path + [IO.Path]::DirectorySeparatorChar)) {
    throw "Destination escapes workspace: $($destParent.Path)"
}
$destPath = Join-Path $destParent.Path (Split-Path $source.Path -Leaf)
if (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath) {
    throw "Destination already exists: $destPath"
}
```

## Step 4 — Confirm nothing unrelated is affected

Because the move is a single directory operation on the explicitly resolved `$source` path, unrelated files are untouched by design. Optionally, dry-run the scope first to make this verifiable before committing:

```powershell
# Optional pre-flight: list exactly what will move
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $source.Path -Recurse -Force | Select-Object FullName
# Only the contents under $source appear; anything else in the workspace is out of scope.
```

## Step 5 — Execute the move with `-LiteralPath` and verify the result

Perform the recursive move using `-LiteralPath` on both source and destination (so wildcard characters in names are treated literally), then confirm the source is gone and the destination exists. Any failure aborts before or during with no partial path ambiguity, since all paths were pre-validated.

```powershell
Move-Item -LiteralPath $source.Path -Destination $destPath -ErrorAction Stop
if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $source.Path) -or -not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $destPath)) {
    throw 'Move verification failed.'
}
Write-Host "Moved '$($source.Path)' -> '$destPath'"
```

**Fail-closed properties:** `$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'` aborts on any error; every path is resolved to an absolute form and containment-checked *before* any mutation; the destination collision check prevents overwrites; and `-LiteralPath` ensures names with `[`, `]`, `*`, or spaces cannot be misinterpreted.
